drivingQuestion: Are trees consecrated together with an ancestral field redeemed separately at their value, or together with the land at fifty shekels per sowing-area?
outcomeNote: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak removes the objection to Rav Huna's identification of the baraita with R' Shimon by grounding R' Yehuda and R' Shimon's ruling in the wording of Leviticus 27:22 rather than in following the time of redemption.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: הִקְדִּישׁ שָׂדֶה מְלֵיאָה אִילָנוֹת, כְּשֶׁהוּא פּוֹדָן — פּוֹדֶה אִילָנוֹת בְּשׇׁוְויָן, וְחוֹזֵר וּפוֹדֶה קַרְקַע בֵּית זֶרַע חוֹמֶר שְׂעוֹרִים בַּחֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כָּסֶף. אַלְמָא קָסָבַר רַב הוּנָא: אָדָם מַקְדִּישׁ — בְּעַיִן יָפָה מַקְדִּישׁ.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» «Rav Huna says:» In a case where one «consecrated a field full of trees, when he redeems» the trees and field, «he redeems» the «trees according to their value, and then redeems» the «land» according to the fixed formula, by which «an area» required «for the sowing of a kor» of «barley» seed is redeemed «for fifty silver shekels.» The Gemara notes that «evidently Rav Huna holds» that when «a person consecrates, he consecrates generously.» In this case he consecrated the trees and the land separately, so that he would have to redeem them each separately, rather than the trees being redeemed as part of the land.

segments.he: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַב הוּנָא: אֶחָד הַמַּקְדִּישׁ בְּחוֹלַת הַמָּחוֹז, וְאֶחָד הַמַּקְדִּישׁ בְּפַרְדֵּיסוֹת סְבַסְטֵי, נוֹתֵן בֵּית זֶרַע חוֹמֶר שְׂעוֹרִים בַּחֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כָּסֶף! אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רְאוּיָה לְפַרְדֵּיסוֹת קָאָמֵינָא.
segments.en: «Rav Naḥman raised an objection to Rav Huna» from the mishna: «Both» one «who consecrates» an ancestral field «in» the low-quality «sands of the» areas «surrounding» the city «and» one «who consecrates» the high-quality «orchards of Sebastia gives» a redemption payment of «fifty silver shekels for» every area required for «sowing a kor of barley» that he consecrated. This indicates that when one consecrates orchards he does not redeem the land and the trees separately. Rav Huna «said to» Rav Naḥman: The mishna is «speaking of» land that «is suitable for orchards» but does not actually have trees planted on it.

segments.he: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: ״בֵּית זֶרַע״ — אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בֵּית זֶרַע, שְׂדֵה גְּפָנִים וּשְׂדֵה קָנִים וּשְׂדֵה אִילָנוֹת מִנַּיִן?
segments.en: Rav Naḥman «raised» another «objection to» Rav Huna from a baraita: When discussing a consecrated ancestral field the Torah states: «“An area fit for sowing”» (Leviticus 27:16). «I have» derived «only an area fit for sowing; from where» do I derive that the same is true for «a field of vines and a field of reeds and a field of trees?»

segments.he: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״שָׂדֶה״ מִכׇּל מָקוֹם, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכָא נָמֵי פּוֹדֶה וְחוֹזֵר וּפוֹדֶה.
segments.en: «The verse states:» “And if a man shall consecrate to the Lord part of the field of his possession, then your valuation shall be according to an area fit for sowing; the sowing of a ḥomer of barley shall be valued at fifty silver shekels” (Leviticus 27:16). The word «“field”» teaches that this halakha applies «in any case,» regardless of the type of field. It can be inferred from here that if one consecrates an orchard, the redemption of the trees is not valued separately from the land. Rav Huna «said to» Rav Naḥman: «Here too,» the baraita means that he first «redeems» the trees «and afterward redeems» the field, according to the formula of the Torah.

segments.he: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: הִקְדִּישׁ שְׁלֹשָׁה אִילָנוֹת מִמַּטַּע עֲשָׂרָה לְבֵית סְאָה — הֲרֵי זֶה הִקְדִּישׁ אֶת הַקַּרְקַע וְאֶת הָאִילָנוֹת שֶׁבֵּינֵיהֶם, כְּשֶׁהוּא פּוֹדֶה — פּוֹדֶה בֵּית זֶרַע חוֹמֶר שְׂעוֹרִים בַּחֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כָּסֶף.
segments.en: Rav Naḥman again «raised an objection to» Rav Huna from a baraita: If «one consecrated three trees» in a field «where ten» trees are «planted in an area required» for sowing «one se’a» of seed [beit se’a], «he has consecrated» not only those trees, but also «the land and the» young «trees between them.» Therefore, if this is his ancestral field, «when he redeems» it, «he redeems» the land and everything contained within it according to the standard rate established by the Torah, where «an area» required «for the sowing of a kor» of «barley seed» is redeemed «for fifty silver shekels.»

segments.he: פָּחוֹת מִיכֵּן, אוֹ יָתֵר עַל כֵּן, אוֹ שֶׁהִקְדִּישָׁן בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה — הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא הִקְדִּישׁ לֹא אֶת הַקַּרְקַע וְלֹא אֶת הָאִילָנוֹת שֶׁבֵּינֵיהֶם.
segments.en: But if the ratio of land to trees was «less than that,» i.e., the trees were planted more densely, «or» if the ratio of land to trees was «more than that,» i.e., the trees were planted less densely, «or if he consecrated» each of the trees separately, «one after the other, this» person «has consecrated neither the land nor the» young «trees between them.» Therefore, when he redeems, he redeems the trees in accordance with their worth.

segments.he: וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ הִקְדִּישׁ אִילָנוֹתָיו, וְאַחַר כָּךְ הִקְדִּישׁ קַרְקַע, כְּשֶׁהוּא פּוֹדֶה — פּוֹדֶה אֶת הָאִילָנוֹת בְּשׇׁוְויֵהֶן, וְחוֹזֵר וּפוֹדֶה קַרְקַע: בֵּית זֶרַע חוֹמֶר שְׂעוֹרִים בַּחֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כָּסֶף!
segments.en: «And moreover, even if one consecrated its trees» when they are planted more densely, or less densely, or one after the other, «and then» afterward «he consecrated» the «land,» so that at this point everything belongs to the Temple treasury, «when he redeems» them, «he redeems the trees» separately «in accordance with their worth, and afterward he redeems» the «land» according to the standard rate, where «an area» required «for the sowing of a ḥomer,» i.e., a kor, of «barley seed» is redeemed «for fifty silver shekels.»

segments.he: וְכִי תֵּימָא: הָכָא נָמֵי פּוֹדֶה וְחוֹזֵר וּפוֹדֶה, הָא מִדְּסֵיפָא פּוֹדֶה וְחוֹזֵר וּפוֹדֶה, מִכְּלָל דְּרֵישָׁא לָא!
segments.en: The Gemara explains the objection: «And if you would say» that «here too,» in the first part of the baraita, it means that he «redeems» the field «and afterward redeems» the trees, «from» the fact that «the latter clause» of the baraita states that «he redeems and afterward redeems, by inference the first clause» is «not» referring to a case where he redeems the field and afterward redeems the trees.

segments.he: אֶלָּא, הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא, דְּאָמַר: מַקְדִּישׁ בְּעַיִן רָעָה מַקְדִּישׁ. דְּתַנְיָא: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ אֶת הַשָּׂדֶה — הִקְדִּישׁ אֶת כּוּלָּהּ. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: לֹא הִקְדִּישׁ אֶלָּא חָרוּב הַמּוּרְכָּב וְסַדַּן הַשִּׁקְמָה.
segments.en: «Rather,» in accordance with «whose» opinion «is this» baraita? «It is» in accordance with the opinion of «Rabbi Shimon, who says» that when one «consecrates,» he «consecrates sparingly. As it is taught» in a baraita: «One who consecrates a field has consecrated all of it. Rabbi Shimon says: He only consecrated a grafted carob» tree «and a sycamore stump.»

segments.he: אִי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, אֵימָא סֵיפָא: וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ הִקְדִּישׁ אִילָנוֹתָיו וְאַחַר כָּךְ הִקְדִּישׁ קַרְקַע, כְּשֶׁהוּא פּוֹדֶה — פּוֹדֶה אֶת הָאִילָנוֹת בְּשׇׁוְויֵהֶן, וְחוֹזֵר וּפוֹדֶה בֵּית זֶרַע חוֹמֶר שְׂעוֹרִים בַּחֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כָּסֶף.
segments.en: The Gemara raises a difficulty: «If» the baraita is in accordance with the opinion of «Rabbi Shimon, say the latter clause: And moreover, even if one consecrates its trees and then» afterward «he consecrated» the «land, when he redeems» them «he redeems the trees» separately «in accordance with their worth, and afterward he redeems» the land according to the standard rate, where «an area» required «for the sowing of a ḥomer» of «barley» seed is redeemed «for fifty silver shekels.»

segments.he: וְאִי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן — לֵיזִיל בָּתַר פִּדְיוֹן, וְלִיפְרְקוּ אַגַּב אַרְעַיְיהוּ, דְּהָא שָׁמְעִינַן לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן דְּאָזֵיל בָּתַר פִּדְיוֹן!
segments.en: «And if» the baraita is according to the opinion of «Rabbi Shimon, let one follow» the status of the field at the time of its «redemption, and let» the trees «be redeemed along with their land,» as at the time of its redemption both the trees and the land are consecrated. «As we have heard that Rabbi Shimon follows» the time of the «redemption,» i.e., he determines the price at which a field is redeemed based on the time it is being redeemed.

segments.he: דְּתַנְיָא: מִנַּיִן לְלוֹקֵחַ שָׂדֶה מֵאָבִיו וְהִקְדִּישָׁהּ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת אָבִיו, מִנַּיִן שֶׁתְּהֵא לְפָנָיו כִּשְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אִם אֶת שְׂדֵה מִקְנָתוֹ אֲשֶׁר לֹא מִשְּׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ״.
segments.en: «As it is taught» in a baraita: «From where» is it derived with regard «to one who purchases a field from his father and consecrated it, and afterward his father dies,» which means that the field would now be his as an inheritance, «from where» is it derived «that it should be» considered «before him as an ancestral field,» rather than a field that he purchased, with respect to its redemption? «The verse states» with regard to a field that was purchased: «“And if» he sanctifies to the Lord «a field that he has bought, which is not of his ancestral fields”» (Leviticus 27:22).

segments.he: שָׂדֶה שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לִהְיוֹת שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה, יָצְתָה זוֹ שֶׁרְאוּיָה לִהְיוֹת שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.
segments.en: The verse speaks specifically of «a field that is not fit» at the time of its consecration «to be an ancestral field,» i.e., one that he could never have inherited in the future. This specification «excludes this» field «that was fit to be an ancestral field» from this halakha, since eventually it would have become his through inheritance, even had he not purchased it. This is «the statement of Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon.»

segments.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִן לַלּוֹקֵחַ שָׂדֶה מֵאָבִיו, וּמֵת אָבִיו, וְאַחַר כָּךְ הִקְדִּישָׁהּ, מִנַּיִן שֶׁתְּהֵא לְפָנָיו כִּשְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה?
segments.en: The baraita continues: «Rabbi Meir» learns a different halakha from this verse and «says: From where» is it derived «that» in a case of «one who purchases a field from his father and his father dies, and» only «afterward he consecrated» the field, «from where» is it derived «that it should be» considered «before him like an ancestral field?»

segments.he: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אִם אֶת שְׂדֵה מִקְנָתוֹ אֲשֶׁר לֹא מִשְּׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּתוֹ״ — שָׂדֶה שֶׁאֵינָהּ שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה, יָצְתָה זוֹ שֶׁהִיא שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה.
segments.en: «The verse states» with regard to a purchased field: “And «if» he sanctifies to the Lord «a field that he has bought, which is not of his ancestral field”» (Leviticus 27:22). The verse is referring specifically to «a field that is not an ancestral field» at the time of its consecration. This requirement «excludes this» field, «as» currently, after the death of the father, «it is an ancestral field.»

segments.he: אִילּוּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וּלְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, אֲפִילּוּ הִקְדִּישָׁהּ וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת אָב — שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה הָוְיָא. מַאי טַעְמָא? אִי מִשּׁוּם קְרָא — קְרָא לְכִדְרַבִּי מֵאִיר הוּא דַּאֲתָא!
segments.en: The Gemara analyzes the baraita. That is the opinion of Rabbi Meir, «whereas» according to «Rabbi Yehuda and according to Rabbi Shimon it is» considered «an ancestral field even if he consecrated» the field «and afterward his father dies. What is the reason» for this opinion? «If» you suggest it is «due to the verse,» that cannot be, as «the verse comes» to teach the halakha that was stated «in accordance» with the opinion of «Rabbi Meir,» i.e., it is referring to a case where the father died before he consecrated the field, as Rabbi Meir explained.

segments.he: אֶלָּא לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּאָזֵיל בָּתַר פִּדְיוֹן?
segments.en: «Rather, is it not due to» the fact «that» he «follows» the status of the field at the time of the «redemption?» Since the father died before the son redeemed the field it is considered an ancestral field in the possession of the Temple treasury. Similarly, if one first consecrates the trees and afterward the field, he should redeem them both together, since at the time of the redemption they are both consecrated. Since this ruling is not in accordance with the baraita that states that the trees and field are redeemed separately, evidently the baraita cannot be in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן קְרָא אַשְׁכַּחוּ וּדְרוּשׁ.
segments.en: «Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said» that this source does not contradict Rav Huna’s claim that the baraita is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon. The reason is that «Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon» do not, in fact, maintain that one follows the status of the field at the time of the redemption. Rather, they «found a verse and expounded it.»

segments.he: אִם כֵּן, לִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא: ״אִם אֶת שְׂדֵה מִקְנָתוֹ אֲשֶׁר לֹא אֲחֻזָּתוֹ״, מַאי ״מִשְּׂדֵה״ — שָׂדֶה שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לִהְיוֹת שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה.
segments.en: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak explains Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon’s reasoning: «If so,» that when one consecrated the field and his father died afterward, it is not considered an ancestral field, «let the Merciful One write» in the Torah: And «if» he sanctifies to the Lord «a field that he has bought, which is not his ancestral,» i.e., the verse could have omitted the repetition of the phrase “of his field.” «What» does the Torah mean by stressing «“of his field”?» This teaches that only «a field that is not fit to be an ancestral field» at the time he consecrated it is redeemed for its value. But if he consecrated a field that he would inherit in the future, it is redeemed in the manner of an ancestral field.

moves.about: what Rav Huna's two-stage redemption reveals about his view of the scope of a consecration

moves.cueHe: אלמא קסבר רב הונא
moves.summary: the Gemara reads out of Rav Huna's ruling that he holds one consecrates generously
moves.about: that one who consecrates consecrates generously (בעין יפה), a principle Rav Huna did not state here

moves.cueHe: איתיביה רב נחמן לרב הונא
moves.summary: Rav Naḥman objects from the mishna's single rate for the orchards of Sebastia
moves.about: whether consecrated orchards are redeemed together with their land at the fixed rate rather than separately

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: ראויה לפרדיסות קאמינא
moves.summary: Rav Huna narrows the mishna to land merely fit for orchards
moves.about: the mishna speaks of land merely suitable for orchards, not of land actually planted with trees

moves.cueHe: איתיביה: ״בית זרע״ — אין לי אלא בית זרע
moves.summary: Rav Naḥman objects from a baraita extending the fixed rate to a field of trees
moves.about: whether a field of trees is redeemed by the fixed sowing-area formula rather than by separate valuation

moves.cueHe: תלמוד לומר ״שדה״ מכל מקום
moves.summary: the baraita derives from the word שדה that every kind of field is redeemed by the formula
moves.about: the word שדה extends the fifty-shekel formula to every kind of field

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: הכא נמי פודה וחוזר ופודה
moves.summary: Rav Huna answers that this baraita too means two successive redemptions
moves.about: the baraita too means that he first redeems the trees and afterward redeems the land

moves.cueHe: איתיביה: הקדיש שלשה אילנות ממטע עשרה לבית סאה
moves.summary: Rav Naḥman objects from the baraita on consecrating three trees with the land between them
moves.about: whether trees consecrated together with their land are redeemed with the land at the fixed rate

moves.cueHe: פחות מיכן, או יתר על כן
moves.summary: the baraita's middle clause: a different spacing consecrates neither land nor the trees between
moves.about: the baraita on consecrating three trees in a densely planted field and how such a consecration is redeemed

moves.cueHe: ולא עוד, אלא אפילו הקדיש אילנותיו
moves.summary: the baraita's latter clause redeems trees separately and then the land

moves.cueHe: דתניא: מנין ללוקח שדה מאביו והקדישה

moves.cueHe: שדה שאינה ראויה להיות שדה אחוזה
moves.summary: R' Yehuda and R' Shimon exclude a field that was fit to become ancestral
moves.about: the phrase אשר לא משדה אחזתו excludes a field that was fit to become ancestral, so it is redeemed as ancestral

moves.cueHe: רבי מאיר אומר: מנין ללוקח שדה מאביו, ומת אביו
moves.summary: R' Meir reads the same verse for a father who died before the consecration
moves.about: whether the verse's exclusion is about a field merely fit to become ancestral or only about one already ancestral when consecrated

moves.cueHe: תלמוד לומר: ״אם את שדה מקנתו אשר לא משדה אחוזתו״
moves.summary: R' Meir's prooftext excludes a field already ancestral at consecration
moves.about: the verse excludes a field that is already ancestral at the moment of consecration

moves.cueHe: מאי טעמא?
moves.summary: why do R' Yehuda and R' Shimon treat it as ancestral even when consecrated first
moves.about: why R' Yehuda and R' Shimon treat the field as ancestral even when consecrated before the father's death

moves.cueHe: אי משום קרא
moves.summary: floats the verse as their ground
moves.about: whether the verse can be the reason for R' Yehuda and R' Shimon, given that it is already used for R' Meir's derivation

moves.cueHe: קרא לכדרבי מאיר הוא דאתא
moves.summary: the verse is already needed for R' Meir's derivation, so it cannot be their ground

moves.cueHe: אלא לאו משום דאזיל בתר פדיון
moves.summary: only the principle of following the redemption is left, which undoes Rav Huna's identification
moves.about: that R' Shimon's ruling here must rest on following the status of the field at the time of redemption

moves.cueHe: אמר רב נחמן בר יצחק: רבי יהודה ורבי שמעון קרא אשכחו ודרוש
moves.summary: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak grounds their ruling in an exposition, saving Rav Huna
moves.about: that the field-from-father baraita does not show R' Shimon follows the time of redemption, so Rav Huna's identification stands

moves.cueHe: אם כן, לכתוב רחמנא: ״אם את שדה מקנתו אשר לא אחזתו״
moves.summary: the superfluous משדה yields their ruling without any principle of following the redemption
moves.about: the superfluous משדה teaches that a field merely fit to be ancestral is redeemed as ancestral
